take_homes: Giving people a tool is not the same as them using it. The old habit is the competitor.
Before I give someone something, ask how he does the job today.
Pick one person and talk to him first, before building anything.

monday.move: Ask one depot manager how he makes the daily delivery report today, step by step. No AI yet.
monday.when: Tuesday, when I am at the depot anyway. Not Monday, the week starts too busy.
monday.stop_condition: If he says it takes 10 minutes and he is fine with it, I drop it.
monday.blocker: No time, and the reporting data sits in a system I cannot export from without IT.

misconception.why: Nothing in the module touched operations. No shift plan, no delivery report, only software-team talk and a consultant story. The 'one person, one question' idea is useful for any change, but I still think AI is a customer chatbot thing.

one_line: Too much text in English, but the point that getting people to actually use a tool is the hard part is true. I would only recommend it to someone who has the patience for the reading.
